newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf reports positive Gulf of Mexico find.
newsitem.headline: Elf reports positive Gulf of Mexico find.

text.p: Elf Aquitaine said on Monday its U.S. oil and gas subsidiary had achieved "positive results" from a deepwater oil and gas discovery on the Virgo Prospect in the Gulf of Mexico.
An extended test on the Viosca Knoll 823-2 well, drilled down to a depth of 4,060 metres, produced a maximum daily flow of 22.7 million cubic feet of gas and 1,816 barrels of oil.
The well, begun on March 26, encountered a total of 115 net metres of hydrocarbon bearing sands, Elf said in a statement on behalf of its Elf Exploration Inc subsidiary.
The well is the first drilled by the French oil company in a new Gulf of Mexico strategy focusing on deepwater oil finds.
A second well is planned for July and a decision on whether it justifies commercial development could be taken later this year, it said.
The Virgo Prospect consists of four blocks of the Viosca Knoll region, located offshore Louisiana and covering 93 square kilometres.

Elf Exploration Inc is the operator with a 64 percent interest in association with Coastal Oil and Gas Corp (which has 16.2 percent), Pogo Producing Company (10.8 percent) and Nippon Oil Exploration USA Ltd (nine percent).
Elf says it has increased its deepwater acreage in the Gulf of Mexico from three blocks in 1995 to 41 blocks at present.
